content.title: What is the Collections Framework?
content.description: The Java Collections Framework (JCF) is a unified architecture that provides interfaces, implementations, and algorithms to efficiently store, manipulate, and process groups of objects.

content.content: Arrays have a fixed size and limited functionality. The Java Collections Framework (JCF) provides dynamic data structures such as lists, sets, queues, and maps that can grow or shrink during program execution. It also offers powerful utility methods for searching, sorting, and manipulating collections.

content.title: Why Learn Collections?
content.content: Collections are used extensively in Java applications for managing data efficiently and are one of the most frequently tested topics in coding interviews.
Core Interfaces
The Collections Framework consists of several interfaces that define how groups of objects should be stored and manipulated.

rows: Processes elements in insertion order or priority.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Collection is the root interface for List, Set, and Queue, while Map belongs to a separate hierarchy.

content.content: List Interface
The List interface maintains insertion order, allows duplicate elements, and supports index-based access.

content.content: Set Interface
The Set interface stores only unique elements. Duplicate values are automatically ignored.

content.title: HashSet Example
Unique Property
content.content: HashSet automatically removes duplicate entries.
Queue Interface
The Queue interface is designed for processing elements in FIFO (First-In, First-Out) order, although some implementations use priorities.

content.title: Queue Example

content.content: Map Interface
The Map interface stores data as key-value pairs. Keys are unique, while values may be duplicated.

Collections Utility Class
The Collections class provides static utility methods for sorting, searching, reversing, and shuffling collections.

Applications

items.question: Inventory Systems
items.answer: Store unique product IDs using sets.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Library Organization
content.content: A List is like books placed in order on a shelf, a Set is like a collection of unique book IDs, a Queue is like people waiting to borrow books, and a Map is like a catalog that links each book ID to its title.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Collections Framework is one of the most important Java interview topics. Candidates are expected to know List, Set, Map, Queue, ArrayList, LinkedList, HashMap, HashSet, TreeMap, TreeSet, and the Collections utility class.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Is Map a subtype of Collection?
items.answer: No. Map belongs to a separate hierarchy.

items.question: Should ArrayList always be used?
items.answer: No. Choose the implementation based on the application's requirements.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Choose List for ordered data, Set for unique data, Queue for processing order, and Map for key-value storage.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Collections Framework manages groups of objects.
List maintains order and allows duplicates.
Queue processes elements in FIFO or priority order.
Collections utility class provides sorting and searching methods.
